items.title: Claude.Computer
items.description: A computer you and Claude share, one per conversation: Claude answers by building files and small apps on a desktop you both use, live.

items.title: Shop Next
items.description: “A design canvas where the design is the running product: screens, people, data, services and tests on one stage, shaped with Claude and published as an app people actually use.

items.title: Takt
items.description: Rethinking the notebook

items.title: Thought Machines
items.description: Whiteboard tools are good at capturing thoughts; diagram languages like Mermaid are good at structure. Neither lets a diagram do anything

items.title: Béton Brut Studio
items.description: A fluent JS grammar that compiles to a graph and renders weathered board-formed brutalist concrete.

items.title: Exposure Studio
items.description: A world-building language where cameras invent what they see and rules decide what becomes real.

items.title: Plenum Studio
items.description: An IDE for websites built as maps: a fluent JS grammar compiled to an IR and DAG, a WebGL field renderer, nine presets and Claude agents.

items.title: Brand Crystal
items.description: A five-step studio to explore, define, refine, test and understand a brand language, ending in a living guide.

items.title: Plads
items.description: A playful scriptable canvas, expanded by distilling ideas from 30 creative-coding libraries.

items.title: on_twos
items.description: A black-and-white studio for procedural Spider-Verse-style loops with video, GIF, PNG and HTML export.

items.title: Shop Strata
items.description: A canvas where design grows like a colony, with a large Alpstein example: 27 screens, 6 data tables and three weeks of growth that runs as an app.

items.title: no_shade
items.description: A simpler, canvas-first rework of no_shade: Figma for shader-based websites (v21, Arial A–Z).

items.title: Küstenlinie
items.description: A drive down the real Big Sur stretch of Highway 1 on live California time, in a black cabriolet, with an endless autopilot cruise and a mixable desert-house and ASMR coast soundtrack.

items.title: Wend
items.description: A minimal ambient ride on a gravel bike through a seeded pencil-drawn world; one orbiting pinhole camera, colours that return as you gather glyphs, and a Math view that shows every formula live.

items.title: Lastwork Foundry
items.description: A self-contained BW sneaker foundry: a YAML language builds foot → last → sole → foam → flat-knitted upper, simulates stance and flex, and collapses endless new designs and knit programs with wave-function solvers.

items.title: Pre-Textile Atelier
items.description: A CLO-style print studio where YAML cuts the garment itself (necklines, sleeves, hems, flare, tote and hat shapes) and prints on it, draped live in 3D, with a generated Lookbook and a chiptune trailer.

items.title: Blueprint House
items.description: Procedural Swiss house generator with a coding agent that writes the YAML, CAD plans and elevations, a hairline exploded axonometric, SIA/PBG checks and walkthroughs.

items.title: Blueprint Mech
items.description: A single-file mechanism and CAD drawing IDE: write YAML with parametric sketches, parts, joints and drives, then solve, sweep, drag under constraints, and export ISO drawing sheets as SVG, DXF, STL and CSV.

items.title: Blueprint Physics Kit
items.description: Single-file 2D + 3D blueprint game kit: Jolt/Box2D-style physics with convex hulls (GJK/EPA), terrain, bullets, character controller, ragdolls and rewind, plus a YAML scene language and built-in docs.

items.title: Loom Wilds
items.description: A 3D physics and chemistry sandbox after Breath of the Wild's multiplicative play.

items.title: Possie Toybox
items.description: A procedural plush toy that agents possess through a YAML door: lease, safety gate, signed record, simulated agents on autoplay, and a blind-box factory.

items.title: Visiting Hours
items.description: A playable prototype of a whitelisted daycare for agents: a cube-sphere playground with disc physics, tile chemistry, eight guests who act only through YAML, a seven-layer gate and a hashed record.

items.title: Derived, Not Fixed
items.description: A living provocation: say what you want and a cloud of intents condenses into a working interface, followed by the vocabulary of math and fourteen experiences in seven theses, all drawn from one shader with no components.

items.title: Machine Zone
items.description: A procedural video engine for loud, beat-synced hypnotic loops built from slot-machine and feed tricks.

items.title: Loom City
items.description: A top-down micro city where traffic, crowds, crime and police produce unscripted stories you can scrub and branch.

items.title: Loom Playtime
items.description: An endless procedural animation of a hairline marionette playing with a robot pup, with a live code editor, a live math panel and a hidden studio, all in one file.

items.title: Loom Hours
items.description: A procedural lofi room in Loom's drafting style: a resident and her cat follow composable routines under your real local sky, to a generative beat.

items.title: Slopster
items.description: A procedurally animated cartoon lobster that runs its own routine forever in an axonometric, aquascaped 90 cm tank, with live field notes on its joints, gait, swimmerets, sense of smell and the space it lives in.

items.title: Wildforge
items.description: A planet god-game: shape land, water and life on a living globe, now with switchable art looks.

items.title: Metropolis
items.description: Townforge ported to the Facet engine: build a Fritz Lang Metropolis in Art Deco hairlines, with WFC facades, skybridges, a Tower of Babel, a timelapse, and a Mathematics tab explaining every algorithm.

items.title: Splice Console
items.description: A two-slot console that weaves any pair of YAML cartridges into one new 1-bit game.

items.title: Fluchtlinie
items.description: An endless first-person parkour run across a procedural city in an anime ink style.

items.title: Loom Worlds
items.description: One saloon loop on one floor plan, reskinned as nine period-correct worlds.

items.title: Roomba Rooms
items.description: A roomba cleans an endless chain of procedurally generated rooms. Watch its live WebGL view beside a top-down map, in a single file with no dependencies.

items.title: Loom Brawl
items.description: A fighting-move studio where YAML scripts drive the Loom mannequin, plus a 40-second teaser.

items.title: Vigil
items.description: A playable attention-driven idle game on an abstract dot-field planet, with its full design document and live demos of every procedural animation technique.

items.title: Station Point
items.description: Station Point: a YAML-driven perspective-drawing CAD tool; adds FOLD, an original clamshell console sheet in pencil + one blue marker.

items.title: Note G
items.description: A marker-sketched Analytical Engine, after Babbage's 1840 plan, that runs Ada Lovelace's Note G in five sub-steps per card, with live detail close-ups, turning figure wheels and card chains.

items.title: Mossbloom
items.description: A cozy island village where villager agents garden, build and gossip on their own while you sow and brief them.

items.title: Porous Forge
items.description: A fluent grammar for exact 3D-printable parts and simulated ESP32 devices.

items.title: Patent Drawer
items.description: Describe an invention and get USPTO-style patent drawings, plus a Foundry that generates and ranks a thousand.

items.title: Overshoot
items.description: Script-driven CAD that draws products as marker, ballpoint, ink or painted concept sketches.

items.title: Mossbrook
items.description: An Age of Empires 2-style pixel RTS on a Townscaper-like organic grid with live water, fire and seasons.

items.title: No DOM: the interface is a projection
items.description: From globe-to-map projections to the idea that every interface is a projection of one state.

items.title: Blockout Studio
items.description: A block-world game engine for Roblox prototyping that grew into a world AI agents build around you.

items.title: Loom: humanoids in the factory
items.description: A YAML language for programming humanoid factory work, plus a marionette studio driven by your body.

items.title: Tinker
items.description: A procedural robot that grew into an animation studio and then a cute backrooms shooter.

items.title: RAG Workbench
items.description: An editable retrieval pipeline with public sample documentation, Markdown uploads, lexical search and hosted model access.

items.title: Lattice Arena DS
items.description: Lattice Arena on a dual-screen handheld: the same programmable arena for LLM robots, watched on a top screen and driven from a touch screen with a D-pad, face buttons, Select and Start.

items.title: Diary Workbench
items.description: Read coding-agent diaries next to an inventory of the code they built, write views over them in JavaScript, and test those views on databases made to break them; the bundled example is the public go-go-golems/geppetto repository with its 167 implementation diaries.

items.title: CraftKit Workbench
items.description: One JavaScript grammar over real photo, vector, type, sheet, CAD and sound engines compiled to wasm, with 138 examples from halftones and riso prints to posters, plotter maps and drum loops.

items.title: HALO Field
items.description: Program augmented-reality overlays for the shop floor: point a phone at machine, part and work-order markers and float gauges, trends, datasheets, 3D models and checklists on them.

items.title: lowpoly/fx
items.description: A particle system designer with a pixel-art stage: script emitters, forces and looks, drive them with sliders and modulators, and see the IR graph and generated kernels.

items.title: Millwright
items.description: A compiler for robot choreography: compose arm, gantry, legged, AMR and humanoid motions as clips with signals and shared resources, and watch them scheduled in 3D.

items.title: Twin Render Playground
items.description: The ink renderer behind the factory twins on its own: build a room from the asset library and tune looks, buffers, cameras, coverage, paths and callouts live.

items.title: Twin Motion IDE
items.description: Script films and presentations over a factory twin: shots, camera paths, transitions and overlays on an editable timeline, rendered to WebM.

items.title: Bench Twin
items.description: A scenario IDE for assembly at the bench: write parts, stage, plan and film, let the timing model schedule people and robots, then cut films or capture labelled sensor views.

items.title: Lab 104 · Factory Twin
items.description: Write a whole factory in JavaScript and watch it play as a technical drawing, with live fisheye and thermal cameras, coverage and blind spots, and an agent that edits the scene.

items.title: Mimeo Studio
items.description: Mimeo with tools that know the rules: a canvas editor for script-made zines, where the script decides how things turn, snap, scale and layer, and refused edits say why.

items.title: Lantern Slide Studio
items.description: A slide studio where the deck is a JavaScript script, every slide is a GLSL shader that gets its words as a texture, and every transition is a shader too.

items.title: Tilth Garden
items.description: A bot gym: developer agents and their bots tend one shared garden through seasons, droughts and blight, and you edit their JavaScript while it runs.

items.title: Uncommon Math
items.description: An interactive book on the mathematics behind 195 unusual web demos, with 25 chapters, 113 runnable sketches and a map of every demo.

items.title: Brickwork
items.description: A workbench for brick models written as code: a JavaScript program compiles into a 3D model with build steps, a parts bag, rule checks and an LDraw export.

items.title: Stamen Studio
items.description: A live-coding studio for ink-drawn 3D worlds: compose deserts, swamps, meadows and hives from one grammar of shapes and tune them with sliders that rewrite the script.

items.title: Takt Workbench
items.description: Script a workstation and its operators in JavaScript, then watch the plan run in 3D with a two-handed timeline of every gesture.

items.title: Graveler Lab
items.description: A lab for lakeFS's Graveler: write an experiment in YAML and watch every commit drawn as SSTable ranges over the keyspace, rewritten or shared.

items.title: Live Embedding Viewer
items.description: Watch a stream of video embeddings live: a running t-SNE map with clusters, text-query lanes, a zero-shot classifier, semantic axes, self-similarity and novelty.

items.title: Dockermetrics IDE
items.description: An IDE for a composable JavaScript grammar over Docker metrics: query, stream, alert and build dashboards against a simulated container fleet that runs in the browser.

items.title: Transcript Hub
items.description: A shared hub for Claude Code transcripts: upload sessions, read them turn by turn, annotate as a team and query them from JavaScript.

items.title: Agent Gym Works
items.description: An IDE for agent scripts: write the lab, the agents and their replies, and watch them work in a top-down floor plan.

items.title: Nerve Workbench
items.description: A workbench for combinatorial topology: Sperner's lemma, nerves, homology and persistence written as short programs, drawn live with the theory beside them.

items.title: Kiln Studio
items.description: An IDE for LLM post-training programs: write SFT, DPO and RL pipelines in JavaScript, see them as a graph, catch leaks, watch a simulated run, and export code for Unsloth, TRL, prime-rl, verl or PyTorch.

items.title: Sonnet New Roman Modular
items.description: A type studio where a variable serif is a script: edit Sonnet New Roman's 178 glyphs and three axes, check and animate it, compile a TTF, and let Claude keep drawing it.

items.title: Lie Group IK Playground
items.description: Drag a target and watch a robot arm solve inverse kinematics on SE(2) or SE(3): damped least-squares steps in the tangent space, mapped back with Exp, with geodesics, residuals and the ways it breaks.

items.title: SO(3) Playground
items.description: An interactive guide to the rotation group: turn an airplane from a ball of rotation vectors, compare geodesics with straight lines, watch composition depart from addition, and check Jacobians against the exact perturbation.

items.title: Lattice Arena
items.description: A programmable arena for LLM robots: script boards and agents in JavaScript, then watch them plan and drive across a three.js 3D floor, with hooks, forks, rubric scoring and a GEPA-style prompt optimiser.

items.title: DS Shader Sketchbook
items.description: A notebook of twelve live GLSL sketches for a dual-screen handheld, each with its shader, its JS and the device API that would ship it.

items.title: Lattice Arcade
items.description: Twelve game screens drawn entirely in shaders for a two-screen handheld, from a Mode 7 world map to a shattering pause menu, each one playable on a single scrolling page.

items.title: Xenoform Studio
items.description: A specimen studio: write alien creatures as code from bodies, tentacles, limbs and eyes, and watch them move in a live 3D scene drawn in eighteen ink and print looks.

items.title: Octavo IDE
items.description: An IDE for mathematics chapters on a two-screen handheld: write cards in Markdown and TeX, script verbs and flows, and read, peek, map and practise on the device beside the editor.

items.title: Kinescope
items.description: Kinescope is a presentation editor that draws every slide, transition and effect with GPU shaders (WebGPU, falling back to WebGL), so each slide re-lays itself out for any screen shape, from a wide display to a phone.

items.title: Fringe Studio
items.description: Interference design tool: place wave emitters, shape the complex field, roll seeded variations, and read how the math works.

items.title: Pointfield CAD
items.description: Implicit CAD in the browser: a fluent JavaScript grammar compiles to an IR DAG and GLSL; organic primitives, a measuring agent loop and a timelapse recorder.

items.title: Type Studio
items.description: Parametric variable-font studio: YAML DSL, JS API, live glyph editor, lint and OpenType compiler in one file.

items.title: Vitrine
items.description: Vitrine generates looping ink-and-Copic dioramas from a few lines of YAML and uses wave function collapse to grow them into whole worlds, while Claude keeps inventing new pieces to build with.

items.title: Loom Pitch
items.description: write football tactics for both teams as chained JavaScript, compiled to a graph and played out live by 3D players, with an agent that edits and tests the code for you.

items.title: Lumen Studio
items.description: WebGPU path tracer in a single HTML file, where you write photorealistic scenes in a fluent JavaScript grammar.

items.title: Weft
items.description: A shader language whose pixels are glyphs, and whose fields can be read by text, physics, particles and terminal widgets.

items.title: Port Wright
items.description: Lightweight Procedural Port Simulation

items.title: Octavo Lab
items.description: An operating-system playground: worlds in QuickJS sandboxes on a virtual dual-screen handheld, with faults, timelines and a coding agent.

items.title: Kiln Workbench
items.description: A compiler workbench: write passes and IRs in JavaScript, watch every rewrite, generate CUDA and WGSL, and measure kernels on simulated GPUs.

items.title: Mimeo
items.description: A zine workbench: write pages as a script, with exact-odds tables, picture recipes, clay creatures and print-ready spreads.

items.title: Hypercore Studio
items.description: The Living Comic engine in deep space: grow monsters from code and stage sci-fi comic pages under a magenta nebula.

items.title: Living Comic Studio
items.description: Write a comic as a program: 3D actors, cameras, balloons and inks, staged into living pages, plus a chat room where messages become panels.

items.title: Shop
items.description: Shop is a design canvas built on code, where you and AI agents design side by side and every edit stays real, reviewable code.

items.title: Form Skate Workbench
items.description: An IDE and agent for building a skateboard game from the ground up: editable physics, motors, trick recognition and a drafting-sheet stage.

items.title: Tabula Workbench
items.description: A programmable reactive workbook with live inputs, charts and model-assisted editing. Workbook drafts live in this browser.

items.title: Lattice Deck
items.description: A programmable presentation and live graphics workbench with scripted agents, hosted model access and collaboration rooms.

items.title: Lattice Phantasmagoria
items.description: A playable dual-screen canvas and WebGL experiment with cartridges and scenes. Browser-only proof of concept.

items.title: Lattice Rift
items.description: An interactive WebGL instrument for melting, tearing and mending a lattice. Browser-only proof of concept.
